# `Q-3-20` — Block Metadata Not Supported

> YAML metadata blocks are internal AST nodes that cannot be
> rendered in this output format.

## What this means

Quarto represents document-level YAML (the `---` front matter)
and block-level metadata fences as their own AST node type. The
render pipeline normally consumes these nodes *before* they reach
the writer — front matter becomes document metadata, block
metadata is attached to the block it annotates, and the
metadata-as-node form disappears.

This error fires when a `BlockMetadata` node survives to the
writer. The writer has nowhere to put it: it is structurally a
block, but its content is YAML, not prose.

## Why this happens

Most often a Lua filter, or another non-default processing path,
left a metadata block in the AST when it should have consumed or
attached it. The error is defensive — the normal pipeline does
not produce this shape.

## How to fix

Identify the filter or processing step that introduced the
orphan metadata. If a filter is creating `BlockMetadata` nodes
deliberately, either consume them within the filter or rewrite
them into a representation the writer can render (a `RawBlock`,
for example).

If no custom filter is in use, report the document at the Quarto
issue tracker — the pipeline should not leave block metadata
behind.

  metadata-shape problem, but at the document level rather than
  the block level.
